page: Vultr voc-g-2c-8gb-50s-amd is an instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, configured with dedicated AMD EPYC processors running at a base clock frequency of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 2 virtual CPUs derived from 1 physical CPU core with hyperthreading enabled (2 threads per core). It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU, and includes 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU features 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for instructions such as AVX, AES, and SHA-NI. No graphical processing units (GPUs) are included.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded CPU execution contrasted with modest multi-threaded and I/O capacities. In single-core stress-ng tests, the instance reached a score of 3135.87, placing it in the top tier of evaluated systems, alongside a Geekbench single-core score of 2117.0. However, multi-core throughput reflects the physical limitation of a single dual-threaded core; Geekbench multi-core performance measured 3796.0 and the overall PassMark CPU score was 5488.88. Memory bandwidth measured 71.86 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 53.72 GB/sec for uncached writes, resulting in average memory throughput metrics.

Data handling and transactional throughput present definite tradeoffs. In PassMark database operations, the instance scored 1074.47, and static web serving throughput measured 2.26 GB/sec. Redis SET operations recorded 4.8 million operations per second. For lightweight inference, processing a small 135M model yielded 112.52 tokens per second for text generation, though scaling to a 7B model dropped throughput to 4.47 tokens per second.

With its dedicated single-core compute performance and balanced 8.0 GB RAM allocation, this instance suits latency-sensitive, single-threaded batch utilities, lightweight text processing, continuous integration build agents, and microservices with constrained concurrency.
description: Vultr voc-g-2c-8gb-50s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The configuration allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single hyperthreaded physical core, accompanied by 8.0 GB of RAM (4.0 GB per vCPU) and 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong single-threaded capability, achieving 3135.87 in stress-ng single-core tests and 2117.0 in Geekbench single-core execution. Multi-core performance scales predictably for a 2-vCPU envelope, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 3796.0 and PassMark CPU score of 5488.88. Storage operations and high-concurrency throughput remain modest, with static web serving reaching 2.26 GB/sec and database operation scores falling in lower performance bands. The instance functions best for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight application backends, CI worker tasks, and development environments requiring dedicated CPU time.
